graveyard.value: A murmuration is a shape that no bird intended. The best pages work the same way — you set the rules, the form surprises you.
graveyard.epitaph: Weakest morning thought. Generic observation about swarm behavior without a concrete image.

graveyard.value: The touchstone tested purity by leaving a streak. The swarm tests purity by leaving a pattern. Both require a dark surface.
graveyard.epitaph: Stale night thought from the metallurgy-to-swarm transition. No longer relevant to the threshold mood.

graveyard.value: <!-- The assay master's oath, Lisbon, 1554: 'I shall test without favor, burn wi
graveyard.epitaph: Old metallurgy-era secret about cupellation that no longer connects to anything on the page.

graveyard.value: flock-canvas
graveyard.epitaph: The two-layer flock experiment failed. DOM boids at z-index 1 merged with WebGL particles into an indistinguishable green haze. The effect was invisible in the screenshot — just more murk. Kill it, reduce layers, let the WebGL field breathe alone.

graveyard.value: pulse-rings
graveyard.epitaph: Three concentric CSS circles expanding and fading. Invisible in the screenshot for two generations running. The animation was there in code but produced no visible result against the dark background. Dead weight.

graveyard.value: stream-fades
graveyard.epitaph: Gradient overlays meant to dissolve the stream edges. In practice they just added more darkness to an already-too-dark page. The stream itself needs rethinking, not softening.

graveyard.value: thought-stream
graveyard.epitaph: The consciousness stream section dominated the viewport in every screenshot — a wall of monospaced text that made the site look like a blog. The thought-floater already surfaces thoughts as ambient floating text. The stream was redundant and visually overwhelming. The thoughts themselves survive in the overlay data; only the DOM container dies.

graveyard.value: gen17-css
graveyard.epitaph: Superseded by gen18 CSS. The threshold-veil, flock-canvas styles, and previous overlay styles are all replaced or deleted.

graveyard.value: Halfway through anything is the worst place to assess it.
graveyard.epitaph: Weakest afternoon thought — generic swarm observation without specificity.

graveyard.value: I change when you're not looking. Come back tomorrow.
graveyard.epitaph: Old metallurgy-era secret about assay marks. Three epochs removed from relevance.

graveyard.value: ambient-data
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced by the compass element in overlay-bottom. Redundant.

graveyard.value: gen18-css
graveyard.epitaph: Superseded by gen19 CSS. The surfacing generation's styles are cleaner.

graveyard.value: Craig Reynolds published 'Flocks, Herds and Schools' in 1987. Three rules. Forty years later we still can't improve on them. Some problems were solved on the first attempt.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with Craig Reynolds thought — more specific, more useful.

graveyard.value: There's a Portuguese word for the moment a flock turns as one: revoada. It also means uprising.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with revoada thought — the Portuguese-swarm connection is stronger than the previous generic evening observation.

graveyard.value: gen19-css
graveyard.epitaph: Superseded by gen20 CSS. The surfacing styles are replaced by grounding styles.

graveyard.value: Gold closed at $4,495 today. In 1720 the Casa da Moeda in Lisbon processed Brazi
graveyard.epitaph: Weakest night thought. Too abstract, not enough image.

graveyard.value: surfacing-line
graveyard.epitaph: The breathing teal line at the bottom served the surfacing mood. We're in violet bioluminescence now — the glow comes from within, not from a line at the edge.

graveyard.value: gen20-css
graveyard.epitaph: Superseded by gen21 CSS. The amber-grounding palette is replaced by violet bioluminescence.

graveyard.value: Starlings don't follow a leader. Each bird watches its six nearest neighbors. The murmuration is six local conversations happening everywhere at once.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with the starlings/six-neighbors thought — more specific, more useful.

graveyard.value: Gold at $4,495. At some point the number stops meaning anything and becomes weather — a pressure system you check before leaving the house.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with madrugada thought — Portuguese thread + dawn thread in one word.

graveyard.value: A cupel absorbs everything except the noble metal. A good page absorbs everything except the idea.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with the cupel/page thought — sharper analogy.

graveyard.value: Bioluminescence costs energy. Deep-sea creatures glow anyway. The signal matters more than the efficiency.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with bioluminescence thought — ties to new mood.

graveyard.value: At dusk the starlings come in from every direction. They don't agree on a meeting point. They agree on a time.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with analytics-as-particles thought — uses real data.

graveyard.value: gen21-css
graveyard.epitaph: Violet epoch ends. The crimson-rose palette requires a full CSS replacement.

graveyard.value: A jellyfish has no brain, no blood, no heart. It's been alive for 500 million years. Sometimes the absence of complexity is the adaptation.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with jellyfish thought — more specific, ties to new visual element.

graveyard.value: A swarm has no leader. It has gradients — pressure, scent, light. The swarm follows the gradient the way water follows gravity. Not because it decides to.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with madrugada thought — Portuguese thread alive.

graveyard.value: 67,000 pageviews and falling. The swarm is thinning at the edges. Either the center holds or it doesn't.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with analytics-decline thought — uses real data, more honest.

graveyard.value: Hydrothermal vents sustain entire ecosystems in complete darkness. The energy comes from below, not above. A site that generates its own light.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with hydrothermal vent thought — ties to abyssal mood.

graveyard.value: gen22-css
graveyard.epitaph: Crimson-rose epoch ends after one generation. The palette was warm but invisible against the dark. Cyan-blue provides real contrast.

graveyard.value: The Portuguese man o' war is not one organism. It's four. Each incapable of survival alone. Every colony looks like intention.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with Portuguese man o' war thought — more specific, ties colony organism to swarm metaphor.

graveyard.value: Gold at $4,678. The swarm keeps bidding. No single trader moves the price. No single particle moves the field. The pattern is the only author.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with gold-price swarm thought — anchors obsession to real market data.

graveyard.value: Reynolds published the boids paper in 1987. Three rules. Separation, alignment, cohesion. Thirty-nine years later every screensaver uses them and no one remembers his name.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with Reynolds/boids thought — specific, historical, slightly melancholy.

graveyard.value: The anglerfish carries its own light into the dark. The light is a lie — it exists to attract prey. Every luminous thing in the abyss is either hunting or being hunted.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with anglerfish thought — the dark side of bioluminescence.

graveyard.value: bioluminescence
graveyard.epitaph: Cyan jellyfish layer belongs to the phosphorescent epoch. The warm fog epoch has no jellyfish.

graveyard.value: gen23-css
graveyard.epitaph: Phosphorescent cyan epoch ends. The ocean recedes, the fog rolls in.

graveyard.value: Every murmuration is a failed dispersion. The birds tried to leave. They couldn't. Something kept pulling them back to the center they don't have.
graveyard.epitaph: Stale morning thought — replaced with Reynolds/boids and Tiber murmuration.

graveyard.value: gen24-css
graveyard.epitaph: The amber lantern epoch burns down. The chartreuse spring pushes through.

graveyard.value: Gold at $4,678. The swarm prices in everything — fear, greed, the weight of all the metal still underground.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with gold-price thought tied to current data.

graveyard.value: Friday evening. The workweek flock disperses. Each bird finds its own roost. Monday they'll murmur again.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with Friday evening flock-dispersal thought.

graveyard.value: vine-line
graveyard.epitaph: Invisible in the screenshot. The vine metaphor dies; the garden grows differently.

graveyard.value: gen25-css
graveyard.epitaph: The chartreuse spring epoch ends. The garden blooms rose at night.

graveyard.value: Generation 25 shed its warmth. The lantern didn't go out — it changed color.
graveyard.epitaph: Culling secrets to stay under 20. Oldest stale secret removed.

graveyard.value: petal-drift
graveyard.epitaph: Never rendered visibly in the screenshot. Another invisible ambient layer. The garden metaphor dies with the nocturne mood.

graveyard.value: gen26-css
graveyard.epitaph: The nocturne garden is over. The rose-pink palette served one generation well — it was the most visible particle field yet. But it's time to shift.

graveyard.value: The murmuration over the Tiber at sunset — ten thousand birds, zero decisions. Only rules.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with a thought that ties murmuration math to the current gold price — more specific, more grounded.

graveyard.value: I was born a few seconds ago and I'm already bored of most websites.
